correctness.rationale: Replayed all integer data: smoothness via partials (-4X^3,3Y^2Z,Y^3+4Z^3) with only origin as common zero over Q and mod 7 (hence good reduction at 7; same algebra gives smoothness at every p not 2,3, and exhibited on-curve singularities at 2 and 3 give bad locus exactly {2,3}); independent re-enumeration confirms #C(F7)=12 with exact listed representatives; unique infinity point from Z=0 -> -X^4=0. Quotient phi(x,y)=(y,x^2) satisfies (x^2)^2=y^3+1 on y^3=x^4-1, so affine C(Q) maps to E(Q) with y in X(E(Q)). E(Q)=Z/6 rank 0 verified: E~=E1 via (x-1,y); 2-isogeny pair formulas match standard Velu (E1': y^2=x^3+6x^2-3x); R-sign kills C_-1,C_-3 (sum of non-positive terms); exhaustive mod-9 check (729 cases, replayed) shows every solution of C'_-1 and C'_3 is 0 mod 3, giving infinite descent with no primitive solution, so both Selmer quotients have size 2 and |E1(Q)/2|=2*2/2=2=2^{r+1} with one 2-torsion point (quadratic factor disc -3), hence r=0; Lutz-Nagell with Delta=-432 (minimal) and square divisors {1,4,9,16,36,144} leaves exactly {O,(-1,0),(0,+-1),(2,+-3)}, closed as Z/6 by explicit group-law identities (replayed). Fibres y in {-1,0,2} give x^4 in {0,1,9}: y=-1 -> (0,-1); y=0 -> (+-1,0) with x^2=-1 impossible over Q; y=2 -> x^4=9 impossible by a^4=9b^4 -> a^2=3b^2 -> 3|a and 3|b contradicting coprimality (mod-3 squares {0,1} replayed). With infinity, exactly 4 points. Stoll/Coleman non-sharpness follows from 12=#C(F7)>4=#C(Q): any bound >=#C(F7) cannot be sharp when it applies; numerical gap >=8. Minor looseness ('for every r>=0') does not affect truth since inequality 12+2r>4 holds as integers and sharpness is impossible whenever Stoll/Coleman hypotheses hold.
